title: Maximum 69 Number
statement: The positive integer `num` is written using only the digits 6 and 9. You may flip at most one of its digits, turning a 6 into a 9 or a 9 into a 6, or flip nothing. Return the largest number you can end up with.
constraints: Every digit of num is 6 or 9
notes:
## Intuition

Turning a 9 into a 6 only makes the number smaller, so the only useful move is turning one 6 into a 9. That adds `3` times the digit's place value, so the gain is largest for the 6 in the highest place. Greedy: flip the leftmost 6, or nothing if there is none. Trying every flip (the brute force) gives the same answer with more work.

## Approach

1. Walk the digits from the ones place upward, with `rest` holding the digits not yet read and `place` the value of the current position.
2. Whenever the current digit `rest % 10` is 6, record `place` in `highestSix`. Later (higher) 6s overwrite earlier ones, so at the end it holds the place value of the leftmost 6.
3. Drop the digit with `Math.floor(rest / 10)` and multiply `place` by 10.
4. Return `num + 3 * highestSix`. When there is no 6, `highestSix` stays `0` and `num` is returned unchanged.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = 9669`. Reading from the right: the ones digit is 9; the tens digit is 6, so `highestSix = 10`; the hundreds digit is 6, so `highestSix = 100`; the thousands digit is 9. The answer is `9669 + 3 * 100 = 9969`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(d), where d is the number of digits (at most 4 here).
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Flipping the first 6 found from the right is wrong: in `9669` that gives `9699`, not `9969`.
- Only one flip is allowed; replacing every 6 overshoots.
- A number made only of 9s must come back unchanged, not with a 9 turned into a 6.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rest` | the digits of `num` not yet examined |
| `place` | place value of the digit `rest % 10` (1, 10, 100...) |
| `highestSix` | place value of the highest 6 seen so far, or 0 |

narration.3: No 6 has been seen yet, so the gain is zero for now.
narration.4: Copy num so its digits can be peeled off from the right.
narration.6: Keep reading digits until none are left.
narration.7: Is the current lowest digit a 6?
narration.8: Yes: remember its place value; a higher 6 found later will replace it.
narration.10: Drop the digit that was just examined.
narration.11: The next digit sits one place higher.
narration.14: Turning that 6 into a 9 adds three times its place value; with no 6 this adds nothing.
